overall_summary: Deduplication reveals 47 unique uploads. Extreme exoplanet hazards and first-person 'What If You Fell Into...' simulation hooks represent 100% of the channel's top performers (averaging 700-1,000+ views with peak engagement up to 3.7% like ratio), whereas abstract neuroscience, repeated psychology tips, and generic biology trivia consistently stall under 100 views. Recent velocity heavily favors high-stakes cinematic cosmic scenarios timed around 19-21 seconds.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Hazard Simulation ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: IYuce8vaU3Y (1,029 views, 38 likes), 8KEl0_pJ_68 (972 views, 18 likes), and YlDuGu1vzAg (824 views, 15 likes) drove the channel's highest view counts and like rates.
winning_patterns.action: Frame extreme astronomy and planetary physics through visceral second-person survival and body-consequence simulations.

winning_patterns.evidence: vWd0uYcEGh4 (Burning Ice, 1,057 views) and v1rrcZLdp4U (Darker Than Coal, 1,031 views, 36 likes) outperform standard fact recitations by 5x-10x.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor titles and visual hooks around mind-bending physical contradictions and extreme environmental states.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' posted across three IDs showed diminishing returns (220 -> 87 -> 34 views); 'Fake Memories' repeated with negligible reach (5-53 views).
weak_patterns.action: Halt duplicate subject posting; iterate on proven hook mechanics rather than recycled topics.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Is Hiding This' (38 views), 'Songs Stuck In Your Head' (17-71 views), and 'Fake Memories' (5-53 views) show near-zero subscriber pull and flatline engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Retire isolated cognitive psychology facts in favor of cinematic survival or extreme physical phenomena.
